text:
Nikita Kucherov asked out of Tampa Bay at the end of October. The Associated Press reported he told the Lightning he won't re-sign and wants a trade, and he later said the request stems from disrespect and a lack of communication. General manager Julien BriseBois has said he has no intention of trading him, per Daily Faceoff. So the reigning Hart Trophy winner is playing through a standoff, and Sportsnaut is already asking whether the team's success might change his mind.

On the ice, nothing looks distracted. He has 32 points in 23 games (10 goals, 22 assists), and the Lightning own 60.5% of 5v5 expected goals, the quality of chances, with him out there. If anything he's a touch below his usual level: 3.98 points per 60 against a talent range centred near 4.4 by our numbers, even with the team scoring 7.1 more goals than its chances while he's on. Evolving-Hockey had him second among 401 forwards in wins above replacement last season, with the familiar cost of chances against. Our numbers project about 125 points. Where he scores them is the open question.
headline: Nikita Kucherov keeps producing through a standoff
